title: Father not musical; family plans for the four children
summary: Wooding says his father kept any music to himself, that summers were spent in Atlantic City, and that the children were meant to be dentist, doctor, preacher and nurse.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Mm-huh. And, was he into music at all?

No, I'll tell you. If he was in music, he kept it quiet. I never knew that. And I'll tell you why. How he -- he was a lover of his own people. So, when we heard- I must have been about six or seven years old, when he heard there was a colored show coming to town, he immediately got his wife, my mother, and the four children together and took us to the theater. But, at that time, we were not in Philadelphia, because every summer he worked in Atlantic City at the Brighton Hotel. And by working at the Brighton Hotel, sometimes he had a day off. So, he was a waiter there -- so he said to my mother that he would like for us all to see this show.

Before that, I was supposed to be a dentist, in their mind. My one brother was supposed to be a doctor. My older brother was supposed to be a preacher, and my sister was supposed to be a nurse. But, only two of these things happened. That is, my brother turned into be Cornelius Wooding he turned into be one of the finest doctors in Philadelphia. And I turned out to be a hambone musician in Atlantic City.
